v1.0.0.changelog: Production hardening release: security remediation, backend reliability work, and a gated CI/CD pipeline with migrations and automated backups.

spec.overview: A live AI education platform where the work was production systems engineering: hardening application security, improving backend reliability, and making releases safe.
spec.architecture: Node.js services backed by a relational database through Prisma, running on Linux behind a reverse proxy with process supervision, and shipped through a gated GitHub Actions pipeline that runs migrations and takes automated backups before deploy.

subsystems.name: Application Services
subsystems.function: Node.js backend handling requests, business logic, and production fixes for the live platform.

subsystems.name: Data Layer
subsystems.function: Relational schema and data access managed through Prisma migrations.

subsystems.name: Auth & Access Control
subsystems.function: Secures application endpoints and hardens access paths against production security issues.

subsystems.name: Linux Runtime
subsystems.function: Server, reverse proxy, and process supervision keeping the platform available.

subsystems.name: Release Pipeline
subsystems.function: Gated CI/CD workflow with migrations, automated backups, and a rollback path.

spec.challenges: Fixing security and reliability issues on a live platform without interrupting the users already on it.
spec.engineeringDecisions: Rebuilt the release process around a gated pipeline: review, database migrations, an automated backup before schema changes, and supervised restarts with a defined rollback path.
spec.lessonsLearned: Most production incidents trace back to gaps in the release process rather than to application logic, so the pipeline deserves the same care as the code.
spec.futureImprovements: Run scheduled restore drills so backups are proven recoverable instead of assumed.

interviewQuestions.q: How did you make releases safe on a live system you had inherited?
interviewQuestions.a: I replaced ad-hoc deploys with a gated GitHub Actions pipeline: changes pass review first, Prisma migrations run in order, an automated database backup is taken before any schema change, and services restart under process supervision behind the reverse proxy with a documented rollback path.

replay.title: Security Hardening Pass
replay.description: Audited the live application surface and closed the security gaps that were reachable in production.
replay.decisions: Fixed access-control and input-handling issues at the service layer instead of patching them per route.
replay.challenges: Had to remediate a running platform with real users and existing sessions.
replay.lessons: Security fixes need a staged rollout path, otherwise the fix becomes the outage.

replay.title: Backend Reliability & Workflow Redesign
replay.description: Stabilised backend behaviour and redesigned the workflows behind the critical platform paths.
replay.decisions: Treated recurring failures as design problems, not one-off bugs, and restructured the affected workflows.
replay.challenges: Reproducing production-only failures from logs without a staging replica.
replay.lessons: Error logs plus a clear mental model of the workflow beat guesswork every time.

replay.title: Gated Release Pipeline
replay.description: Replaced manual deploys with a gated CI/CD process covering migrations and backups.
replay.decisions: Automated backups before schema changes and kept the pipeline lightweight to suit a single server.
replay.challenges: Applying migrations safely to live data while keeping downtime near zero.
replay.lessons: A release you can roll back is worth more than a release that is merely fast.
